paragraphs: Rav Yosef son of Rav Ilai.

In [Sukkah 26a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sukkah.26a.11-13), Rav Ashi says, “It is a decree lest he fall asleep.” Hyman comments that this is a scribal error: it should read Rava, from which the wording “Rav Ashi” arose. The Ritva likewise has Rava, while Dikdukei Soferim reads Rav Yosef. Abaye said to him, “But what of the teaching—” Rav Yosef son of Rav Ilai said: “[This refers] to someone who entrusts his sleep to others.” Rav Mesharshiya objected: “Your guarantor needs a guarantor.” Rav Mesharshiya is known to have been Rava’s disciple.[^1][^2]

notes.text: Hyman understands the wording ונעשה מהרב אשי as a corruption from Rava to “Rav Ashi.” The bracketed words explain במוסר שינתו לאחרים, “entrusts his sleep to others”; the dash marks Hyman’s abbreviated question. Rav Mesharshiya’s discipleship is Hyman’s historical assertion.

The William Davidson text of Sukkah 26a:11–13 reads Rav Ashi. The text cataloged as “Ritva on Sukkah 26a” reads Rava, but its version is titled “Chiddushei HaRashba, Sheva Shitot, Warsaw, 1883.” The edition-label discrepancy remains unresolved. Hyman separately reports Rav Yosef as the reading of Dikdukei Soferim.
